units: <cite ref="Nedarim 22b:3">Ned. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>שעֶרְכָּהּ של ארץ ישראל הוא</he> because it (the Book of Joshua) contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel.—Pl. <he>עֲרָכִים</he>, constr. <cite ref="P01381"><he>עֶרְכֵי</he></cite>.
Cant. R. to VI, 4; Pesik. Vayhi, p. 7ᵃ sq. שש ע׳ המשנה, v. מִשְׁנָה.—ע׳ המלחמה order of battle, arrangements proclaimed before the battle (v. מַעַרְכִים).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 8:1:3">Y. Sot. VIII, beg. 22ᵇ</cite> (ref. to Mish.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 8:6">ib. VIII, 6</cite>) <he>אבל בע׳ המ׳ מספקין וכ׳</he> but in connection with the proclamation of the regulations of battle (the Mishnah says only), ‘they have to supply water &c.’ <cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 8:6">Ib.</cite> <he>אף בע׳ המ׳ כן</he> the same is the case with ordinances of battle (they must be proclaimed in Hebrew). Bab.
<cite ref="Sotah 43b:9">Sot. 43ᵇ</cite> <he>אין חוזרין עליו מע׳ המ׳</he> they are not entitled to leave the army on that account.

senses.gloss: valuation, assessment, value of a person or animal dedicated to the sanctuary; vow of value.
units: <cite ref="Arakhin 7b:59">Arakh. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>ואמר עֶרְכִּי עלי</he> if he says, I vow my own value.

<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 4:1">Ib. IV, 1</cite> <he>הע׳ בזמן הע׳</he> the valuation is regulated by the time of the vow (irrespective of the value at the time of paying the vow); <cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 4:4">ib. 4</cite> <he>נותן כזמן הע׳</he> he pays according to the value at the time of the vow.

<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 4:4">Ib.</cite> <he>נותן ע׳ זקן</he> he pays the value of an old man (<cite ref="Leviticus 27:7">Lev. XXVII, 7</cite>); <he>ע׳ ילד</he> the value of a child (ib. 6); a. fr.—Pl. <he>עֲרָכִים</he>, <he>עֲרָכִין</he>. Ib. II, 1 <he>אין בע׳ וכ׳</he> (Var. <he>נֶעֱרָכִין</he>, v. <cite ref="P01375"><he>עָרַךְ</he></cite>) in vows of value nothing is valued at less than a Selʿa &c.; ib. 7ᵇ <he>כל ע׳ שאתה מעריך וכ׳</he> all values which you assess shall be no less than &c. Ib. IV, 1 <he>והע׳ בנערך</he> the vows of value are regulated by the condition of the person whose value is vowed. Ib. III, 1 <he>יש בע׳ להקל וכ׳</he> in the laws regulating the dedication of values there is a lenient and a rigorous side. Ib. 2ᵃ, a. e. <he>כל שישנו בדמים ישנו בע׳ … אינו בע׳</he> he whose person has a value, can vow the value of a person or an animal, but he whose person has no value cannot.
<cite ref="Leviticus 6:23">B’ḥuck. 6</cite> <he>פרשת ע׳</he> the section treating of vows of value.

Ib. בזכות הע׳ אני מציל וכ׳ as a reward for your offerings of values, I will save you &c.; a. fr.—ʿĂrakhin, name of a treatise of Mishnah, Tosefta and Talmud Babli, of the Order of Kodashim.—[ערכין, Gitt. 44ᵃ Ar., v. עַרְכִי.]
